N° 05Static security analysis for AI-generated web applications2026

CYVAREN

A static analyser for web applications produced with AI coding tools. It parses the source without executing it, evaluates six security properties and reports each finding with its file, line, rationale, remediation and verification step.

Visit the site ↗How to useIn motion

01

Problem statement

AI coding tools reduce the path from idea to deployment to a few hours, and the same speed reproduces well-known vulnerabilities: records readable by changing an identifier in the address, administrative pages without a role check, credentials committed to source, login forms with no limit on attempts. Existing scanners address security teams; the person who generated the application seldom has the vocabulary to act on their output.

02

Contribution

Six checks are phrased as plain questions, and each returns passed, failed, not tested or inconclusive, together with what the analyser could not observe. Every finding states the file and line, the risk, the remediation and how to confirm it, and can be copied as a prompt for an AI coding tool. An architecture map lists routes, data stores and external services and marks the data paths reachable without authentication; a written walkthrough explains the application for six audiences. Successive scans are compared to show what has been resolved. With AI assistance enabled, Claude explains a finding in the context of the user’s code and drafts a fix in Repair Studio, which CYVAREN re-scans before presenting the diff.

03

Architecture

A TypeScript monorepo comprising a Fastify 5 API with Drizzle ORM on PostgreSQL hosted by Neon, a Next.js 16 and React 19 front end, and a command-line client that runs the same checks in continuous integration. On Vercel the API is mounted inside the web application, and scans run after the response has been returned.

04

Method and data

Uploaded archives and public GitHub repositories are parsed into syntax trees for JavaScript and TypeScript in order to trace routes, guards and data access; secrets are detected by built-in rules, and dependencies are checked against OSV.dev. Nothing in the analysed project is installed or executed. Dependency upgrades are proposed by a deterministic rule rather than by a language model.

05

Verification and limitations

Workspaces are isolated, and tests assert that a request from another workspace receives not found. AI requests reach Anthropic without tool access, with secret values masked and a daily limit per workspace, and assistance stays off until a workspace enables it. Route and guard tracing covers JavaScript and TypeScript, and a static analyser cannot observe runtime configuration, which is why every check states what it could not see.
